transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, can folks see the deck I just dropped in the chat? 
[00:30] Raj Kapoor: Yep, I can see it. Thanks Jamie. 
[01:02] Maya Patel: Hey team, Maya here from Redwood SE. I'll cover the bench—benchmarks and the tech side, especially the dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs. 
[01:20] Lucy Morales: Great, good to meet you Maya. Ok so high level from Nimbus, we have three deals we want to push together this quarter, one strategic enterprise, two midsize. 
[01:45] Jamie Chen: Perfect. Before we jump in, quick alignment: our goal today is to 1) confirm the three target deals, 2) agree owners and outreach cadence, and 3) plan the technical benchmark for the enterprise opportunity. 
[02:14] Ethan Brooks: Quick note, our procurement timeline for the enterprise deal is tight — legal wants SOC2 evidence and KMS integration info by Dec 15. 
[02:35] Maya Patel: Got it. We'll surface our SOC2 package and a KMS integration runbook. Also for the benchmark, we recommend running both hosted API and a Dedicated config to compare latency and cost per 1M tokens. 
[03:03] Raj Kapoor: Sounds good. For the enterprise deal, the prospect is very latency-sensitive; they mentioned 95th percentile under 200ms for chat. 
[03:22] Maya Patel: Okay that maps to our dedicated inference tier, but we can also show hosted with smart routing + KV caching to demonstrate tail latency improvements. Note: KV cache sometimes transcribed as K V cash in our past exports so, heh. 
[03:46] Lucy Morales: The midsize deals are less strict — cost is the big factor. We want to see quantization profiles and expected cost delta vs OpenAI. 
[04:10] Jamie Chen: We'll include Redwood Optimize recommendations + expected unit economics for quantized models. We'll also provide example batching configs. 
[04:32] Ethan Brooks: Do you have any reference numbers for cost per 1M tokens on dedicated vs hosted for a Llama-3 style model? 
[04:50] Maya Patel: Rough numbers: hosted gen is about $X per 1M tokens (we'll fill in exact in the follow-up deck), dedicated can be lower depending on utilization and batching. Important: continuous batching and kernel selection drive most of the savings. 
[05:10] Raj Kapoor: On the partner side, we want co-branded decks and a one-pager for sales that clarifies SLAs and support matrix. 
[05:28] Jamie Chen: We'll share a co-sell one-pager and a partner enablement deck. Also propose a 2-week cadence for joint outreach once Nimbus confirms contacts. 
[05:47] Lucy Morales: For the enterprise legal ask—are audit logs and data residency supported in your Private offering? 
[06:05] Maya Patel: Yes, our Private on-prem or VPC control plane supports audit logs; we have KMS/HSM integrations and can provide artifact for data residency. We'll attach SOC2 artefacts; note that some customers want additional attestations, we can scope that with Legal. 
[06:41] Ethan Brooks: Good. The prospect also asked about SSO and RBAC for admin controls. 
[06:50] Jamie Chen: Redwood supports SAML SSO and granular RBAC. We'll include an admin matrix. 
[07:10] [00:07:10] Speaker 1: so the high level for pipeline, deal A is enterprise healthcare, stage: evaluation; deal B is fintech mid-market, stage: proposal; deal C is e-commerce mid-market, stage: discovery. 
[07:35] Raj Kapoor: Correct. For deal A the technical champion is the head of ML infra, they've asked for a 1-week POC to validate throughput and latency. 
[07:50] Maya Patel: For a one-week POC we'll need access to a sample request trace and representative prompt sets. Ideally we run both a hosted replay and a dedicated run. 
[08:12] Lucy Morales: Is there any risk on your side for running a replay? We can't share PII—need to scrub data. 
[08:26] Maya Patel: Totally, we can provide a replay checklist and scrub guidance. Also we can run synthetic traces if needed. 
[08:40] Jamie Chen: On GTM, Raj, do you want us to co-host a webinar or a joint customer call? 
[08:52] Raj Kapoor: A joint customer intro call would be good, followed by an internal enablement for Nimbus sellers. 
[09:05] Jamie Chen: I'll own the enablement session. Maya will run the tech deep dive/benchmark. 
[09:20] Ethan Brooks: Regarding pricing, the prospect asked about committed reserved capacity discounts — do you have standard tiers? 
[09:33] Jamie Chen: Yes, reserved capacity for Dedicated has monthly/annual commit tiers; we'll share the pricing matrix. Also, there's burst options for sudden load. 
[09:50] [00:09:50] Maya Patel: One engineering note — if they're using on-prem GPU infra we need to align on compilation and kernel selection; model compatibility matters for quantized variants. Sometimes model names in our docs get transcribed oddly — e.g., Llama/Alpaca etc — we'll include a compatibility matrix. 
[10:18] Lucy Morales: For the midsize deals, can you provide self-serve onboarding docs so Nimbus SDRs can demo quickly? 
[10:30] Jamie Chen: Absolutely. We'll share quickstart templates and a demo script. 
[10:44] Raj Kapoor: For the enterprise POC timeline, legal wants an NDA in place before we start any log sharing. 
[10:55] Jamie Chen: We'll push our mutual NDA template; I'll send that after the call. 
[11:10] Ethan Brooks: Any competitors in play on these deals? The enterprise prospect is evaluating Anthropic and Vertex AI. 
[11:20] Maya Patel: Noted. We'll prepare differentiation notes: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, cost controls, and traceable rollout policies. 
[11:38] [00:11:38] Speaker 2: quick question on observability — does Redwood Console expose token-level cost and per-model tracing? 
[11:48] Maya Patel: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, error analysis and tracing hooks. We'll include sample screenshots. 
[12:05] Lucy Morales: On security they also asked about encryption at rest — is that standard? 
[12:15] Maya Patel: Yes, encryption at rest is standard; for Private we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. 
[12:30] Jamie Chen: Ok let's walk the three deals quickly — deal A (enterprise healthcare): key asks are SOC2 evidence, latency POC, and KMS integration. Owner: Raj + Maya. 
[12:52] Raj Kapoor: Yup Raj will lead outreach and provide buyer contacts. 
[13:05] Jamie Chen: Deal B (fintech): stage proposal, need cost comparisons and quantization guidance. Owner: Raj + Jamie. 
[13:20] Lucy Morales: Deal C (e-comm): discovery, wants a demo and self-serve onboarding. Owner: Ethan + Jamie. 
[13:35] [00:13:35] Speaker 3: are there any open technical risks? 
[13:42] Maya Patel: The main risk is network egress and VPC peering timelines for the enterprise POC — that can delay the Dedicated runs. We'll propose a hosted replay in the meantime. 
[13:58] Ethan Brooks: If the VPC peering hits legal, how long is typical to stand up a hosted replay? 
[14:08] Maya Patel: We can stand up a hosted replay within 48 hours once we have scrubbed traces. Dedicated benchmarking takes longer to schedule based on reserved capacity windows. 
[14:28] Raj Kapoor: Ok that's acceptable. 
[14:40] Jamie Chen: Next steps recap — Jamie send co-sell one-pager, Maya schedule benchmark, Raj share opportunities. Any objections? 
[14:55] Lucy Morales: One more ask: can Redwood provide references for a similar healthcare customer who did a Dedicated deployment? 
[15:08] Maya Patel: Yes we have an anonymized reference pack; we'll include case study highlights. 
[15:25] [00:15:25] Speaker 1: awesome. Let's lock on dates — Maya, what's your availability week of Dec 8 for a 90-min deep dive? 
[15:36] Maya Patel: I'm available Tue/Wed morning PST. I'll send a calendar invite. 
[15:47] Jamie Chen: I'll follow up with the enablement calendar too. 
[16:00] Raj Kapoor: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity. 
[16:08] Lucy Morales: Thanks all. 
[16:15] Ethan Brooks: Thanks. 
[16:20] [00:16:20] Jamie Chen: Meeting adjourned — I'll email the NDA and the one-pager in the next 24 hours. 
[16:30] 
Notes: occasional transcription errors present (names slightly off in automated captions), timestamps approximate.
